summary:
ORBIT (Outpost Resource & Base Intelligence Trainer) is a free browser-based game that teaches children aged 7–12 how to manage a Moon outpost for 14 sols (days).

Players control a team of four astronauts and manage limited power across life support, food production, radiation shielding, and science. Every decision has consequences, teaching players the importance of balancing resources to keep astronauts safe and complete their mission.

ORBIT features Real Space Weather Replay, using historical solar flare data from NASA's DONKI database to create realistic emergency scenarios. It also includes educational lessons and real NASA images with proper credits.

By combining interactive gameplay with real space science, ORBIT helps children understand the challenges astronauts and mission planners face. It requires no downloads or accounts and clearly distinguishes real NASA data from simulated game events.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

ORBIT is a free browser game for kids aged 7 to 12. Players command a Moon outpost with four astronauts for 14 sols (days), keeping Oxygen, Food, Shield and Crew Health from running out while reaching a science goal. No download or account is needed.

HOW IT WORKS

Each sol, players split a fixed power budget between Life Support, Food, Shielding and Science. More power for one system means less for another, and arrows show the effect before each choice. A storm forecast arrives one sol early. Emergencies such as solar storms, dusty solar panels and radio blackouts offer choices that each cost power or science. Each one ends with a lesson card containing a real fact, a credited NASA photo and its source.

REAL NASA DATA

Real Space Weather Replay uses solar flare records from NASA/CCMC DONKI: 14 sols map to 14 real dates, and the strongest flare days become the storms. Photos come from the NASA Image and Video Library. [Keep if working: real space biology studies from NASA OSDR appear in an Astronaut Health Lab.] Events and facts are real; game numbers are illustrative and never shown as real radiation doses.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Kids usually see what missions achieve, not how planners decide what to power and protect. ORBIT lets them practice those decisions and learn that every choice in space has a cost.

CREATIVITY

The "no choice is free" rule is built into the mechanics, real flare days drive the storms, and a Mission Journal collects NASA photos and lessons.

FACTORS CONSIDERED

Plain language, accessibility (keyboard, reduced motion, no flashing lights), fair event timing tested across 100 random missions, and honest labeling of real versus simulated data.

TOOLS

React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, three.js, Recharts, Vitest, Node data scripts, Vercel. Code: [GitHub link]. AI tools (Claude, v0, Antigravity) helped write code and text, as disclosed in the app and README.
